page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highcpu-32 is a compute-optimized server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9B45 processor. It features 32 vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 60 GB of dedicated system memory, yielding approximately 1.88 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results show top-tier performance in single-core stress-ng tests, Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression. The processor's extended instruction set capabilities are reflected in strong Passmark CPU and encryption scores, as well as strong multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory bandwidth for both read and write operations falls within the average range, while static web serving throughput is strong. For small language model inference, text generation speed is in the top tier, while prompt processing remains strong.

The primary tradeoff of the c4d-highcpu-32 is its low memory-to-vCPU ratio of under 2 GB per core, making it less suitable for memory-intensive databases or massive datasets. However, its high-density compute allocation provides qualitative cost efficiency for CPU-bound workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. This instance is suited for software compilation, image processing, text processing, ray tracing, and light LLM inference tasks.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highcpu-32 is an x86_64 compute-optimized server featuring 32 vCPUs and 60 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 9B45 processor with 16 physical cores. This instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, focusing resources entirely on dedicated CPU performance. Benchmark data indicates top-tier single-core and multi-core CPU performance, with strong results in software compilation, ray tracing, and text processing. It offers average memory bandwidth and database operation speeds. Given the low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1.88 GB per core, this server is designed for CPU-bound workloads such as software compilation, image processing, and web serving, rather than memory-heavy database applications.
